topics.title: AI basics: what is AI and ML
topics.description: Artificial intelligence is the broad goal of building systems that perform intelligent tasks, while machine learning is a subset that learns patterns from data instead of relying only on hand-written rules.

lessons.title: AI basics: what is AI and ML: The core idea
lessons.body: Artificial intelligence is the broad goal of building systems that perform intelligent tasks, while machine learning is a subset that learns patterns from data instead of relying only on hand-written rules.

lessons.title: AI basics: what is AI and ML: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Use a rule when behavior is stable and explicit; use learning only when patterns and data make it useful.

lessons.title: AI basics: what is AI and ML: A worked example
lessons.body: A thermostat can follow fixed rules, while a model can learn a temperature-to-energy pattern from examples.

lessons.title: AI basics: what is AI and ML: Identify what is learned
lessons.body: Ask which part of a system changes after it sees examples. A fixed rule that flags every payment above a limit is not learned; a fraud model adjusts its parameters from past transactions. Both can belong to a larger automated system.

topics.title: Data types: structured vs unstructured data
topics.description: Structured data follows a fixed schema such as rows and columns, while unstructured data (text, audio, images) needs additional processing before models can consume it effectively.

lessons.title: Data types: structured vs unstructured data: A worked example
lessons.body: A spreadsheet of transactions has named columns; a customer email is text that needs parsing or an embedding before many models can use it.

lessons.title: Data types: structured vs unstructured data: Choose a representation
lessons.body: A support ticket can contain structured fields such as creation time alongside free-text notes and an attached image. Decide how to represent each field separately. Converting the notes into word counts loses word order, while resizing the image can remove small details.

lessons.title: Data types: structured vs unstructured data: Where it can fail
lessons.body: A file extension does not determine meaning: inspect the schema, missingness, and how the information will be represented.

topics.title: Intro to datasets
topics.description: A dataset is a collection of examples used for training and evaluation, typically with features (inputs) and labels (targets) when the task is supervised.

lessons.title: Intro to datasets: Define one example
lessons.body: Specify what one row represents before counting examples. A dataset with ten orders from each of 100 customers has 1,000 orders but only 100 customers. If the goal is to predict behavior for new customers, keep each customer's records together when splitting the data.

lessons.title: Intro to datasets: The core idea
lessons.body: A dataset is a collection of examples used for training and evaluation, typically with features (inputs) and labels (targets) when the task is supervised.

lessons.title: Intro to datasets: A worked example
lessons.body: A row can represent one order, with features known before shipment and a label saying whether it arrived late.

lessons.title: Intro to datasets: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Check how each row was collected and whether train and evaluation examples are independent.

topics.title: Basic math for AI
topics.description: Core AI math includes vectors, matrix operations, and basic algebra because model predictions are usually computed as weighted combinations of numeric features.

lessons.title: Basic math for AI: Calculate a weighted sum
lessons.body: For input vector [2, 3] and weights [0.5, -1], the dot product is 2*0.5 + 3*(-1) = -2. Adding a bias of 4 gives a prediction of 2. Each input must line up with its corresponding weight; swapping feature order changes the calculation.

lessons.title: Basic math for AI: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Keep track of units and dimensions; an invalid shape or scale can make a correct formula meaningless.

topics.title: Intro to statistics
topics.description: Statistics helps quantify uncertainty through concepts like mean, variance, and distributions, which are essential for understanding noisy real-world data.

lessons.title: Intro to statistics: The core idea
lessons.body: Statistics helps quantify uncertainty through concepts like mean, variance, and distributions, which are essential for understanding noisy real-world data.

lessons.title: Intro to statistics: See an outlier's effect
lessons.body: The values 2, 3, 3, 4, and 18 have mean 6 and median 3. The large value pulls up the mean while leaving the median near most observations. Neither summary tells the whole story, so inspect the spread and investigate whether 18 is a valid observation.

lessons.title: Intro to statistics: A worked example
lessons.body: The mean delivery time can hide a long tail, so pair it with a spread measure and inspect the distribution.

topics.title: Visualization basics
topics.description: Visualizations like histograms, scatter plots, and box plots quickly reveal distribution shape, outliers, and variable relationships before modeling begins.

lessons.title: Visualization basics: A worked example
lessons.body: A histogram reveals skew in transaction amounts, while a scatter plot can expose a nonlinear relationship or an outlier.

lessons.title: Visualization basics: Where it can fail
lessons.body: A visual pattern is a hypothesis, not proof of cause or reliable predictive signal.

lessons.title: Visualization basics: The core idea
lessons.body: Visualizations like histograms, scatter plots, and box plots quickly reveal distribution shape, outliers, and variable relationships before modeling begins.

topics.title: Data inspection
topics.description: Initial data inspection checks missing values, duplicates, data types, and unrealistic ranges to prevent avoidable modeling errors.

lessons.title: Data inspection: Investigate suspicious records
lessons.body: A negative age could indicate a parsing error, a special missing-value code, or a broken source system. Inspect the raw record and field definition before replacing it. Record the cause and count affected rows so a recurring ingestion problem does not go unnoticed.

lessons.title: Data inspection: The core idea
lessons.body: Initial data inspection checks missing values, duplicates, data types, and unrealistic ranges to prevent avoidable modeling errors.

lessons.title: Data inspection: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Summaries can hide duplicates and subgroup issues; sample actual records as well as aggregate counts.

lessons.title: Data inspection: A worked example
lessons.body: Count missing values, verify a date column parses correctly, and inspect extreme quantities before training.

topics.title: Intro to predictions
topics.description: A prediction is a model output produced from input features, such as a class label, a probability, or a continuous numeric estimate.

lessons.title: Intro to predictions: Separate output from action
lessons.body: Suppose a delay model returns 0.3. With a notification threshold of 0.2, the system sends an alert; with a threshold of 0.5, it does not. The prediction is unchanged. The action also depends on the policy and the cost of unnecessary or missed alerts.

lessons.title: Intro to predictions: Where it can fail
lessons.body: A score is not a guarantee or action by itself; check calibration and the cost of each decision.

lessons.title: Intro to predictions: The core idea
lessons.body: A prediction is a model output produced from input features, such as a class label, a probability, or a continuous numeric estimate.

lessons.title: Intro to predictions: A worked example
lessons.body: A delivery model might return a delay probability of 0.3; a separate threshold determines whether the system flags the order.

topics.title: Supervised vs unsupervised
topics.description: Supervised learning trains with labeled targets, while unsupervised learning finds latent structure such as clusters or low-dimensional representations without labels.

lessons.title: Supervised vs unsupervised: Match the question to the data
lessons.body: To learn which requests need escalation, supervised training needs examples with escalation targets. If those labels do not exist, clustering can help explore recurring request types, but a cluster number is not an escalation prediction. Human review may help turn that exploration into a labeling plan.

lessons.title: Supervised vs unsupervised: A worked example
lessons.body: Predicting a known churn label is supervised; grouping users without labels is exploratory unsupervised learning.

lessons.title: Supervised vs unsupervised: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Clusters do not come with business meaning; validate whether the groups are stable and useful.

topics.title: Feature vs label
topics.description: Features are the inputs provided to a model, and the label is the ground-truth value the model is trained to predict.

lessons.title: Feature vs label: A worked example
lessons.body: For a house-price task, floor area available at listing time is a feature and the eventual sale price is the label.

lessons.title: Feature vs label: The core idea
lessons.body: Features are the inputs provided to a model, and the label is the ground-truth value the model is trained to predict.

lessons.title: Feature vs label: Spot a leaked answer
lessons.body: When predicting whether an order will arrive late at checkout, the eventual delivery timestamp cannot be an input: it reveals the outcome after the decision. Use information already known at checkout as features, and derive the late-delivery label from the later delivery record.

topics.title: Data cleaning basics
topics.description: Data cleaning standardizes formats, handles nulls, removes duplicates, and corrects inconsistencies so the model learns from reliable signals.

lessons.title: Data cleaning basics: Distinguish missing from zero
lessons.body: A missing purchase amount means the amount is unknown; zero can mean a valid free order. Replacing every missing amount with zero erases that distinction. Investigate why values are absent, choose a documented handling rule, and retain a missingness indicator when it carries useful information.

lessons.title: Data cleaning basics: The core idea
lessons.body: Data cleaning standardizes formats, handles nulls, removes duplicates, and corrects inconsistencies so the model learns from reliable signals.

topics.title: Simple classification idea
topics.description: Classification maps an input to one of several classes, for example spam vs not spam, often using probabilities and a decision threshold.

lessons.title: Simple classification idea: The core idea
lessons.body: Classification maps an input to one of several classes, for example spam vs not spam, often using probabilities and a decision threshold.

lessons.title: Simple classification idea: A worked example
lessons.body: A spam filter estimates whether a message belongs to spam or legitimate mail, then applies a threshold to the score.

lessons.title: Simple classification idea: Where it can fail
lessons.body: The best threshold depends on the harm of missed spam versus blocking an important message.

lessons.title: Simple classification idea: Count both kinds of error
lessons.body: In spam detection, a false positive blocks legitimate mail and a false negative lets spam through. Count the two separately rather than reporting only the percentage of correct predictions. A filter that labels every message legitimate can look accurate when spam is rare while catching none of it.

topics.title: Simple regression idea
topics.description: Regression estimates a continuous value such as demand or price and is evaluated with error-based metrics like MAE or RMSE.

lessons.title: Simple regression idea: Measure numeric error
lessons.body: If predicted demand is 12 units and actual demand is 9, the absolute error is 3 units. Mean absolute error averages this distance across predictions and keeps the target's units. Compare it with a simple forecast such as the previous week's demand to judge whether the model adds value.

lessons.title: Simple regression idea: The core idea
lessons.body: Regression estimates a continuous value such as demand or price and is evaluated with error-based metrics like MAE or RMSE.

lessons.title: Simple regression idea: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Use a time-based holdout to avoid future information leaking into training and communicate forecast uncertainty.

topics.title: AI workflows
topics.description: A practical AI workflow moves from problem framing and data preparation to training, evaluation, deployment, and continuous monitoring.

lessons.title: AI workflows: A worked example
lessons.body: Frame the decision, establish a baseline, audit the data, evaluate on a held-out set, then deploy with monitoring.

lessons.title: AI workflows: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Do not move to a more complex model until evidence shows the simpler approach misses the need.

lessons.title: AI workflows: Plan the feedback loop
lessons.body: For a delivery-delay service, record each prediction with its model version and match it to the eventual arrival outcome. That feedback lets the team detect deteriorating performance. Decide who investigates a rise in missed delays and whether the response is a data fix, retraining, or rollback.

lessons.title: AI workflows: The core idea
lessons.body: A practical AI workflow moves from problem framing and data preparation to training, evaluation, deployment, and continuous monitoring.

topics.title: AI use cases
topics.description: Common AI use cases include recommendation, fraud detection, forecasting, language understanding, and visual inspection in production systems.

lessons.title: AI use cases: Check whether learning is useful
lessons.body: A demand forecast needs historical demand and a planning decision that benefits from it. If a fixed reorder rule already meets the need, a learned forecast may add maintenance without improving outcomes. Start with a use case where errors can be measured and the prediction can change a decision.

lessons.title: AI use cases: The core idea
lessons.body: Common AI use cases include recommendation, fraud detection, forecasting, language understanding, and visual inspection in production systems.

lessons.title: AI use cases: A worked example
lessons.body: Fraud review, demand forecasting, and image inspection have different labels, error costs, and latency needs.

topics.title: Linear regression
topics.description: Linear regression models a continuous target as a weighted sum of features and is a strong baseline for interpretable numeric prediction tasks.

lessons.title: Linear regression: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Linearity is an assumption to examine; a strong training fit does not ensure the relationship holds outside the sample.

lessons.title: Linear regression: The core idea
lessons.body: Linear regression models a continuous target as a weighted sum of features and is a strong baseline for interpretable numeric prediction tasks.

lessons.title: Linear regression: Read the residuals
lessons.body: A residual is the observed target minus its prediction. Plot residuals against predicted values: a curved pattern suggests missing nonlinear structure, while a widening spread suggests changing error variance. These patterns guide investigation even when the average error appears acceptable.

lessons.title: Linear regression: A worked example
lessons.body: Estimate apartment rent from area and location, then plot residuals to see whether errors vary by neighborhood.

topics.title: Logistic regression
topics.description: Logistic regression transforms a linear score into a probability and is commonly used for binary classification with a clear decision boundary.

lessons.title: Logistic regression: A worked example
lessons.body: A logistic model can rank applications by default probability; a threshold maps those scores to a review action.

lessons.title: Logistic regression: The core idea
lessons.body: Logistic regression transforms a linear score into a probability and is commonly used for binary classification with a clear decision boundary.

topics.title: Train/test split
topics.description: A train/test split keeps one partition unseen during training so final metrics reflect how the model behaves on new data.

lessons.title: Train/test split: A worked example
lessons.body: For a future-demand task, train on earlier dates and reserve a later period as the final test.

lessons.title: Train/test split: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Repeatedly selecting features after viewing test results turns the test set into validation data.

lessons.title: Train/test split: Keep related records together
lessons.body: If several images come from the same object, a random image split can put near-duplicates in both partitions. Split by object when evaluating performance on unseen objects. Fit preprocessing on the training partition only, then apply those fitted transformations to the test data.

topics.title: Basic metrics
topics.description: Classification metrics such as precision, recall, and F1 complement accuracy, while regression uses MAE, MSE, or RMSE depending on error sensitivity.

lessons.title: Basic metrics: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Accuracy can look high when one class dominates; choose metrics based on error consequences.

lessons.title: Basic metrics: A worked example
lessons.body: For missed fraud, recall may matter; for costly investigations, precision may matter. Report both with the confusion matrix.

lessons.title: Basic metrics: The core idea
lessons.body: Classification metrics such as precision, recall, and F1 complement accuracy, while regression uses MAE, MSE, or RMSE depending on error sensitivity.

lessons.title: Basic metrics: Calculate precision and recall
lessons.body: Suppose a fraud detector flags 20 transactions, of which 15 are fraudulent, and there are 30 fraudulent transactions overall. Precision is 15/20 = 75%; recall is 15/30 = 50%. The first measures how often an alert is right, and the second measures how much fraud it catches.

topics.title: k-NN algorithm
topics.description: k-NN predicts using the labels of nearby examples, so performance depends strongly on distance scaling and the choice of k.

lessons.title: k-NN algorithm: A worked example
lessons.body: A k-NN model predicts a new flower from nearby labeled flowers; centimeters should not be overwhelmed by millimeters.

lessons.title: k-NN algorithm: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Distance-based predictions depend on scaling, the choice of k, and the density of training examples.

topics.title: Decision trees
topics.description: Decision trees recursively split features into rules, making predictions easy to explain but often requiring pruning or ensembles to avoid overfitting.

lessons.title: Decision trees: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Unrestricted depth can memorize records; constrain growth and validate the resulting rules.

lessons.title: Decision trees: Control small leaves
lessons.body: A leaf containing one training record can make a very confident prediction from almost no evidence. Increasing the minimum samples per leaf prevents some of these fragile rules. Choose that setting with validation data and inspect whether important rare cases still receive useful predictions.

lessons.title: Decision trees: A worked example
lessons.body: A tree might first split by account age and then by recent activity to route a transaction for review.

topics.title: Data preprocessing
topics.description: Preprocessing includes normalization, encoding categorical values, and handling missing data so model inputs are consistent and learnable.

lessons.title: Data preprocessing: Handle unseen categories
lessons.body: An encoder fitted on training cities may later receive a city it has never seen. Decide whether to map it to an unknown category or use an encoding that tolerates unseen values. Save the fitted encoder with the model so training and serving use the same column order and mappings.

lessons.title: Data preprocessing: A worked example
lessons.body: Fit an imputer and category encoder on training folds, then apply those fitted transforms to validation examples.

topics.title: Feature engineering
topics.description: Feature engineering creates informative inputs from raw data, such as ratios, time features, or domain-derived aggregates that improve model signal.

lessons.title: Feature engineering: Build a historical aggregate
lessons.body: For a purchase at noon, a 'spend in the last seven days' feature must stop at noon and exclude the current target outcome. Recreate that time boundary for each training example. An aggregate computed from the full customer history can accidentally include future purchases.

lessons.title: Feature engineering: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Domain features can encode leakage or fragile assumptions; document how they are produced at serving time.

lessons.title: Feature engineering: A worked example
lessons.body: For a timestamped purchase, derive hour-of-day and time-since-last-order using only events available then.

lessons.title: Feature engineering: The core idea
lessons.body: Feature engineering creates informative inputs from raw data, such as ratios, time features, or domain-derived aggregates that improve model signal.

topics.title: Clustering basics
topics.description: Clustering groups similar samples without labels, helping with segmentation, anomaly exploration, and dataset understanding.

lessons.title: Clustering basics: A worked example
lessons.body: Cluster support requests by text representation, then read examples from each cluster before assigning labels.

lessons.title: Clustering basics: Examine what defines a group
lessons.body: If requests cluster mostly by message length rather than subject, the representation may emphasize the wrong similarity. Read typical and borderline examples from each group. Compare assignments across resamples or initializations before treating a cluster as a stable customer segment.

lessons.title: Clustering basics: The core idea
lessons.body: Clustering groups similar samples without labels, helping with segmentation, anomaly exploration, and dataset understanding.

topics.title: PCA basics
topics.description: Principal Component Analysis projects data to lower dimensions while preserving maximum variance, useful for compression and denoising.

lessons.title: PCA basics: The core idea
lessons.body: Principal Component Analysis projects data to lower dimensions while preserving maximum variance, useful for compression and denoising.

lessons.title: PCA basics: Choose the number of components
lessons.body: Inspect cumulative explained variance to see how much variation the retained components preserve. If PCA feeds a predictor, also measure validation performance: retaining 95% of feature variance does not guarantee retaining the information needed for the target. Fit centering, scaling, and PCA only on training data.

lessons.title: PCA basics: Where it can fail
lessons.body: The highest-variance directions may not preserve the target signal or make components easy to interpret.

lessons.title: PCA basics: A worked example
lessons.body: PCA can compress correlated sensor measurements into a few orthogonal components for visualization.

topics.title: Pipeline basics
topics.description: ML pipelines chain preprocessing and modeling steps into one reproducible workflow, reducing leakage and training-serving inconsistencies.

lessons.title: Pipeline basics: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Transformations fitted before splitting can leak information even if the classifier itself is trained correctly.

lessons.title: Pipeline basics: The core idea
lessons.body: ML pipelines chain preprocessing and modeling steps into one reproducible workflow, reducing leakage and training-serving inconsistencies.

lessons.title: Pipeline basics: A worked example
lessons.body: A pipeline keeps imputation, scaling, and estimation together so cross-validation refits each step correctly.

topics.title: Overfitting concept
topics.description: Overfitting occurs when a model learns noise from training data, causing strong train performance but weak generalization to unseen examples.

lessons.title: Overfitting concept: The core idea
lessons.body: Overfitting occurs when a model learns noise from training data, causing strong train performance but weak generalization to unseen examples.

lessons.title: Overfitting concept: A worked example
lessons.body: A tree with near-perfect training accuracy but much lower test accuracy has likely learned sample-specific detail.

topics.title: Cross-validation
topics.description: Cross-validation rotates validation folds to estimate performance more reliably and to compare models with less split-to-split variance.

lessons.title: Cross-validation: A worked example
lessons.body: Rotate the held-out fold across several partitions to compare model settings without depending on one lucky split.

lessons.title: Cross-validation: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Grouped or temporal data needs a split strategy that respects its structure rather than random folds.

lessons.title: Cross-validation: The core idea
lessons.body: Cross-validation rotates validation folds to estimate performance more reliably and to compare models with less split-to-split variance.

lessons.title: Cross-validation: Interpret fold variation
lessons.body: Scores of 0.91, 0.90, 0.89, 0.72, and 0.90 deserve more investigation than their mean alone suggests. Inspect the low-scoring fold for population differences or scarce classes. Use the same folds to compare candidates so differences do not merely reflect easier partitions.

topics.title: Model evaluation workflow
topics.description: A good evaluation workflow defines metrics upfront, checks baseline comparisons, inspects error patterns, and validates assumptions before deployment.

lessons.title: Model evaluation workflow: Where it can fail
lessons.body: A single aggregate metric can hide leakage, subgroup failures, or an unacceptable error type.

lessons.title: Model evaluation workflow: The core idea
lessons.body: A good evaluation workflow defines metrics upfront, checks baseline comparisons, inspects error patterns, and validates assumptions before deployment.

lessons.title: Model evaluation workflow: Audit errors by slice
lessons.body: After computing the overall metric, separate errors by meaningful slices such as new versus returning customers. Include each slice's sample count so a result based on a handful of examples is not mistaken for firm evidence. Use validation errors for iteration and reserve the final test for the selected approach.

topics.title: First ML project
topics.description: A first ML project should prioritize clear problem scope, clean data, a simple baseline, and iterative improvements guided by measurable outcomes.

lessons.title: First ML project: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Do not optimize a model before verifying that the label is meaningful and available at decision time.

lessons.title: First ML project: Make the result reproducible
lessons.body: Save the dataset version, split rule, preprocessing settings, and model configuration with the reported score. Another person should be able to regenerate the result from those records. Record a simple baseline alongside it so the project demonstrates an improvement rather than just a trained model.

lessons.title: First ML project: The core idea
lessons.body: A first ML project should prioritize clear problem scope, clean data, a simple baseline, and iterative improvements guided by measurable outcomes.

lessons.title: First ML project: A worked example
lessons.body: Start with a narrow question, a documented dataset, one baseline, and a result another person can reproduce.

topics.title: Ensemble methods
topics.description: Ensembles combine multiple models to improve robustness and accuracy by averaging or boosting complementary prediction behaviors.

lessons.title: Ensemble methods: A worked example
lessons.body: Averaging diverse models can reduce variance; boosting adds learners to correct earlier errors.

lessons.title: Ensemble methods: The core idea
lessons.body: Ensembles combine multiple models to improve robustness and accuracy by averaging or boosting complementary prediction behaviors.

lessons.title: Ensemble methods: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Ensembling costs complexity and latency; keep it only if held-out performance or reliability improves.

topics.title: Hyperparameter tuning
topics.description: Hyperparameter tuning explores settings like depth, learning rate, and regularization to maximize validation performance without overfitting.

lessons.title: Hyperparameter tuning: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Large searches can overfit the validation set; track the search budget and selection process.

lessons.title: Hyperparameter tuning: Budget the search
lessons.body: Define a search space and a maximum number of trials or training hours before starting. Compare candidates on fixed validation folds and retain their configurations, including unsuccessful trials. When estimating the performance of the entire selection process, nested cross-validation separates tuning from outer-fold evaluation.

lessons.title: Hyperparameter tuning: The core idea
lessons.body: Hyperparameter tuning explores settings like depth, learning rate, and regularization to maximize validation performance without overfitting.

topics.title: Feature selection
topics.description: Feature selection removes redundant or noisy variables, improving interpretability, reducing training cost, and sometimes improving generalization.

lessons.title: Feature selection: The core idea
lessons.body: Feature selection removes redundant or noisy variables, improving interpretability, reducing training cost, and sometimes improving generalization.

lessons.title: Feature selection: Where it can fail
lessons.body: A feature that ranks highly may proxy for a sensitive attribute or leak future information.

lessons.title: Feature selection: Test a smaller feature set
lessons.body: Compare the full model with one trained without an expensive feature group using the same validation folds. A negligible quality change may justify simpler data collection. Correlated features can substitute for each other, so a low individual importance score does not mean the underlying information is useless.

lessons.title: Feature selection: A worked example
lessons.body: Remove redundant variables using selection performed inside each training fold, then compare stability and error.

topics.title: Bias-variance tradeoff
topics.description: The bias-variance tradeoff balances underfitting and overfitting: simpler models have higher bias, complex models often have higher variance.

lessons.title: Bias-variance tradeoff: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Bias and variance are diagnostic lenses, not a rule that complexity should always be minimized.

lessons.title: Bias-variance tradeoff: A worked example
lessons.body: A shallow model may miss a real pattern, while a very deep model may follow noise; compare learning curves.

lessons.title: Bias-variance tradeoff: The core idea
lessons.body: The bias-variance tradeoff balances underfitting and overfitting: simpler models have higher bias, complex models often have higher variance.

topics.title: Advanced evaluation
topics.description: Advanced evaluation includes calibration, threshold analysis, subgroup metrics, and cost-aware decision rules for production-relevant model assessment.

lessons.title: Advanced evaluation: Where it can fail
lessons.body: No metric is universally best; report the operational assumptions and uncertainty.

lessons.title: Advanced evaluation: The core idea
lessons.body: Advanced evaluation includes calibration, threshold analysis, subgroup metrics, and cost-aware decision rules for production-relevant model assessment.

lessons.title: Advanced evaluation: A worked example
lessons.body: Choose a threshold using validation costs, inspect subgroup metrics, and calibrate probabilities if decisions use risk.

lessons.title: Advanced evaluation: Account for review capacity
lessons.body: If reviewers can inspect only 100 alerts per day, evaluate precision and recall at that workload rather than choosing a threshold by F1 alone. Include how many cases remain unreviewed and the cost of missed positives. A threshold selected on one population may need reassessment when prevalence changes.

topics.title: Neural networks basics
topics.description: Neural networks stack differentiable layers that transform input features into richer representations learned from data.

lessons.title: Neural networks basics: The core idea
lessons.body: Neural networks stack differentiable layers that transform input features into richer representations learned from data.

lessons.title: Neural networks basics: A worked example
lessons.body: A hidden layer transforms inputs through learned weights and nonlinear activations, allowing richer patterns than a linear map.

lessons.title: Neural networks basics: Where it can fail
lessons.body: More layers do not guarantee better results; compare compute, data needs, and a simpler baseline.

topics.title: Backpropagation
topics.description: Backpropagation computes gradients efficiently from output to input layers, enabling gradient-based optimization of neural network parameters.

lessons.title: Backpropagation: Check a computed gradient
lessons.body: For a small differentiable example, perturb one parameter slightly in each direction and estimate the derivative from the resulting loss difference. Compare it with the backpropagated gradient while holding randomness fixed. A disagreement can reveal a detached computation or an incorrect custom derivative.

lessons.title: Backpropagation: Where it can fail
lessons.body: A gradient tells the local direction of change, not whether the learning rate or model design is appropriate.

lessons.title: Backpropagation: A worked example
lessons.body: Backpropagation applies the chain rule from the loss back through each layer to compute parameter gradients.

topics.title: Deep learning basics
topics.description: Deep learning uses multi-layer neural networks to automatically learn hierarchical features in text, vision, and speech tasks.

lessons.title: Deep learning basics: A worked example
lessons.body: A vision network can learn edges and textures in early layers and combine them into task-relevant patterns later.

lessons.title: Deep learning basics: The core idea
lessons.body: Deep learning uses multi-layer neural networks to automatically learn hierarchical features in text, vision, and speech tasks.

lessons.title: Deep learning basics: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Representation learning still depends on labeled data quality, regularization, and evaluation outside the training set.

lessons.title: Deep learning basics: Diagnose the training run
lessons.body: If both training and validation error remain high, first check labels, preprocessing, and whether optimization is making progress. If training error falls while validation error rises, investigate overfitting. These situations call for different changes; adding layers is not a diagnosis.

topics.title: NLP basics
topics.description: NLP converts human language into machine-readable representations for tasks such as classification, extraction, translation, and generation.

lessons.title: NLP basics: Inspect tokenization
lessons.body: Tokenize a few real messages containing abbreviations, spelling mistakes, and domain terms. Check whether important text is split unexpectedly or lost through truncation. For sentiment classification, removing words such as 'not' can reverse meaning even if the remaining vocabulary looks cleaner.

lessons.title: NLP basics: A worked example
lessons.body: A text classifier turns tokens into representations to identify a topic, while tokenization choices affect rare words.

lessons.title: NLP basics: The core idea
lessons.body: NLP converts human language into machine-readable representations for tasks such as classification, extraction, translation, and generation.

topics.title: Computer vision basics
topics.description: Computer vision models process images with spatial filters to detect patterns such as edges, objects, and scene context.

lessons.title: Computer vision basics: Where it can fail
lessons.body: A model may learn background shortcuts; test on images from different cameras and environments.

lessons.title: Computer vision basics: Verify image preprocessing
lessons.body: Inspect images after resizing, cropping, and normalization rather than only the original files. A crop can remove the object, and an incorrect color-channel order can change the input distribution. Use the same deterministic preprocessing at validation and serving time.

lessons.title: Computer vision basics: A worked example
lessons.body: Convolutional filters detect local image patterns, and deeper layers combine them into object-level signals.

lessons.title: Computer vision basics: The core idea
lessons.body: Computer vision models process images with spatial filters to detect patterns such as edges, objects, and scene context.

topics.title: Time series basics
topics.description: Time series modeling respects temporal order and often uses lags, trends, and seasonality features to forecast future values.

lessons.title: Time series basics: The core idea
lessons.body: Time series modeling respects temporal order and often uses lags, trends, and seasonality features to forecast future values.

lessons.title: Time series basics: A worked example
lessons.body: Predict tomorrow’s demand from earlier observations and calendar signals while preserving chronological order.

lessons.title: Time series basics: Backtest the forecast horizon
lessons.body: For a seven-day forecast, evaluate predictions made seven days before their targets, then move the forecast origin forward through time. Rebuild lag features at each origin using only available history. Compare with a seasonal forecast such as the same weekday's demand from the previous week.

topics.title: Recommendation systems
topics.description: Recommendation systems rank items by predicted relevance using collaborative signals, content features, or hybrid methods.

lessons.title: Recommendation systems: A worked example
lessons.body: Combine item attributes with user-item interactions to rank candidates, then account for cold-start users.

lessons.title: Recommendation systems: Define the candidate set
lessons.body: A ranker cannot recommend an item that candidate retrieval excluded. Evaluate both whether retrieval finds relevant items and whether ranking puts them near the top. Record which items were available at recommendation time; including future or unavailable items makes an offline ranking task unrealistic.

lessons.title: Recommendation systems: The core idea
lessons.body: Recommendation systems rank items by predicted relevance using collaborative signals, content features, or hybrid methods.

lessons.title: Recommendation systems: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Observed clicks reflect exposure and position, not just preference; evaluate bias and coverage.

topics.title: Model deployment basics
topics.description: Deployment packages a trained model behind an API or batch job with versioning, monitoring, and rollback safety.

lessons.title: Model deployment basics: Verify the serving contract
lessons.body: Send a fixed example through both the training-time prediction pipeline and the packaged service, then compare outputs within a defined tolerance. Check missing fields and invalid types too. A successful response is not enough if the service silently uses a different feature order or preprocessing version.

lessons.title: Model deployment basics: A worked example
lessons.body: Package a versioned model behind a bounded API, monitor latency and input quality, and keep a rollback path.

lessons.title: Model deployment basics: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Offline quality does not cover serving failures or distribution changes.

lessons.title: Model deployment basics: The core idea
lessons.body: Deployment packages a trained model behind an API or batch job with versioning, monitoring, and rollback safety.

topics.title: Data pipelines
topics.description: Data pipelines automate ingestion, validation, transformation, and feature generation so training and inference use consistent data logic.

lessons.title: Data pipelines: The core idea
lessons.body: Data pipelines automate ingestion, validation, transformation, and feature generation so training and inference use consistent data logic.

lessons.title: Data pipelines: Handle late and repeated records
lessons.body: An ingestion retry should not double-count the same transaction. Use stable record identifiers and define how corrections or late arrivals update derived features. Keep event time separate from ingestion time so historical training data can reflect what the serving system actually knew at each decision.

topics.title: Model interpretability
topics.description: Interpretability techniques such as feature importance and SHAP explain model behavior for trust, debugging, and compliance.

lessons.title: Model interpretability: Where it can fail
lessons.body: An attribution describes model behavior under its assumptions; it does not establish causality.

lessons.title: Model interpretability: A worked example
lessons.body: Use feature attribution to debug an individual prediction, then verify the explanation under a suitable method.

lessons.title: Model interpretability: Question the reference
lessons.body: An attribution method may compare a prediction with a chosen background population. Changing that reference can change which features appear influential. State the reference and inspect correlated inputs before interpreting an attribution as a stable explanation of an individual prediction.

topics.title: Deep learning architectures
topics.description: Different architectures specialize in different data modalities: CNNs for images, transformers for sequences, and recurrent variants for temporal patterns.

lessons.title: Deep learning architectures: The core idea
lessons.body: Different architectures specialize in different data modalities: CNNs for images, transformers for sequences, and recurrent variants for temporal patterns.

lessons.title: Deep learning architectures: A worked example
lessons.body: A convolutional model suits local image structure, while attention handles long-range relationships in sequences.

lessons.title: Deep learning architectures: Compare under a fixed budget
lessons.body: Train candidate architectures with the same data split and a stated compute budget, then report quality alongside memory and inference latency. A larger model trained much longer is not evidence that its architecture alone is better. Include preprocessing and input resolution in the comparison.

lessons.title: Deep learning architectures: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Choose architecture against modality, data regime, latency, and an empirical baseline.

topics.title: Transfer learning
topics.description: Transfer learning adapts pretrained models to new tasks with less labeled data by reusing representations learned at scale.

lessons.title: Transfer learning: A worked example
lessons.body: Fine-tune a pretrained image encoder on a small labeled dataset and compare frozen features with selective unfreezing.

lessons.title: Transfer learning: Measure domain mismatch
lessons.body: Evaluate a frozen pretrained encoder with a newly trained head before unfreezing the network. If the source images differ strongly from the target domain, inspect errors by target subgroup and compare selective fine-tuning. Keep the pretrained model's required input normalization unless the adaptation deliberately changes it.

topics.title: NLP advanced
topics.description: Advanced NLP covers tokenization strategy, attention-based architectures, fine-tuning, and evaluation beyond simple accuracy metrics.

lessons.title: NLP advanced: Evaluate context and meaning
lessons.body: Build examples where negation, long-range references, or domain-specific terms change the correct answer. For extraction, score the required spans or fields rather than only fluent output. Separate failures caused by context truncation from failures on text the model actually received.

lessons.title: NLP advanced: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Aggregate benchmark scores do not reveal robustness across dialects, domains, or prompt formats.

lessons.title: NLP advanced: The core idea
lessons.body: Advanced NLP covers tokenization strategy, attention-based architectures, fine-tuning, and evaluation beyond simple accuracy metrics.

topics.title: Computer vision advanced
topics.description: Advanced vision topics include object detection, segmentation, augmentation policy design, and domain shift handling.

lessons.title: Computer vision advanced: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Check annotation quality and performance under lighting, camera, and demographic shifts.

lessons.title: Computer vision advanced: A worked example
lessons.body: An object detector predicts boxes and classes; segmentation assigns labels at pixel level for a different use case.

lessons.title: Computer vision advanced: Inspect localization quality
lessons.body: For detection, intersection over union divides the overlap area of predicted and reference boxes by their union area. Report detection quality across localization thresholds and object sizes. A model can identify the right class yet place boxes too loosely for a downstream measurement task.

lessons.title: Computer vision advanced: The core idea
lessons.body: Advanced vision topics include object detection, segmentation, augmentation policy design, and domain shift handling.

topics.title: Reinforcement learning
topics.description: Reinforcement learning trains agents to maximize cumulative reward by learning policies from environment interaction.

lessons.title: Reinforcement learning: A worked example
lessons.body: An agent learns a policy from environment feedback, where reward design shapes which behavior is reinforced.

lessons.title: Reinforcement learning: The core idea
lessons.body: Reinforcement learning trains agents to maximize cumulative reward by learning policies from environment interaction.

lessons.title: Reinforcement learning: Evaluate a policy separately
lessons.body: Evaluate a fixed policy on separate environment seeds without letting evaluation update it. Report the distribution of episode returns and constraint violations, not only the best episode. In a simulator, vary dynamics to check whether the policy exploits an artifact that may not hold outside training.

lessons.title: Reinforcement learning: Where it can fail
lessons.body: A high proxy reward can be gamed; constrain unsafe exploration and inspect behavior, not reward alone.

topics.title: Generative AI
topics.description: Generative AI models learn data distributions to create new content such as text, images, or audio that follows observed patterns.

lessons.title: Generative AI: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Plausibility is not factuality, provenance, or permission to reuse training content.

lessons.title: Generative AI: The core idea
lessons.body: Generative AI models learn data distributions to create new content such as text, images, or audio that follows observed patterns.

topics.title: Large language models
topics.description: LLMs are transformer-based models trained on massive corpora to perform reasoning, retrieval-augmented tasks, and controlled generation.

lessons.title: Large language models: Test grounded answers
lessons.body: For document question answering, include questions the supplied documents cannot answer. Check whether claims are supported by the cited passages and whether the system abstains when evidence is missing. Test retrieval and generation separately: a fluent answer can hide a failure to retrieve the relevant source.

lessons.title: Large language models: A worked example
lessons.body: An LLM generates token sequences conditioned on context and can use retrieval or tools when a product supplies them.

lessons.title: Large language models: The core idea
lessons.body: LLMs are transformer-based models trained on massive corpora to perform reasoning, retrieval-augmented tasks, and controlled generation.

lessons.title: Large language models: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Fluent text is not evidence; evaluate groundedness, privacy, and task success.

topics.title: MLOps
topics.description: MLOps applies software engineering discipline to ML systems through CI/CD, reproducible training, monitoring, and governance.

lessons.title: MLOps: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Automation should not bypass review, rollback, or ownership for a high-impact model.

lessons.title: MLOps: Trace a released model
lessons.body: A model registry entry should identify the training data version, source revision, configuration, and evaluation report. Promote a specific artifact rather than retraining an untracked copy for production. A rollback must restore compatible preprocessing and feature definitions as well as model weights.

topics.title: Distributed training
topics.description: Distributed training splits data and computation across multiple devices to reduce training time for large models.

lessons.title: Distributed training: The core idea
lessons.body: Distributed training splits data and computation across multiple devices to reduce training time for large models.

lessons.title: Distributed training: Where it can fail
lessons.body: More devices may not improve throughput if communication or input loading becomes the bottleneck.

lessons.title: Distributed training: A worked example
lessons.body: Data parallel workers process batches and synchronize gradients, trading wall time for communication overhead.

topics.title: AutoML
topics.description: AutoML automates model search, feature processing, and tuning to speed up baseline creation while preserving reproducibility.

lessons.title: AutoML: The core idea
lessons.body: AutoML automates model search, feature processing, and tuning to speed up baseline creation while preserving reproducibility.

lessons.title: AutoML: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Search can leak validation data or consume a large budget; document the search space and holdout.

lessons.title: AutoML: Audit the selected pipeline
lessons.body: Inspect the winning pipeline's transformations, feature dependencies, and inference cost before accepting it. Verify that preprocessing and feature selection were fitted inside the training folds. Export the exact selected artifact and compare it with a manually specified baseline under the same evaluation protocol.

topics.title: Graph neural networks
topics.description: Graph neural networks propagate information across node neighborhoods, making them effective for relational data like networks and molecules.

lessons.title: Graph neural networks: The core idea
lessons.body: Graph neural networks propagate information across node neighborhoods, making them effective for relational data like networks and molecules.

lessons.title: Graph neural networks: Define what the graph reveals
lessons.body: In a transductive task, unlabeled test nodes and their edges may be visible during training; an inductive task instead evaluates unseen nodes or graphs. State which setting matches deployment. For future-link prediction, exclude edges created after the prediction time from the message-passing graph.

lessons.title: Graph neural networks: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Graph edges can leak labels across splits; define temporal or entity-aware evaluation boundaries.

topics.title: Multimodal AI
topics.description: Multimodal models align and fuse modalities such as text and images to solve tasks requiring cross-modal understanding.

lessons.title: Multimodal AI: A worked example
lessons.body: A vision-language system combines an image with text, but needs tests for missing or contradictory modalities.

lessons.title: Multimodal AI: Verify paired inputs
lessons.body: Check that each caption or transcript corresponds to the correct image or audio segment before training. Compare the fused model with each single-modality model, then evaluate mismatched and missing inputs. This reveals whether useful cross-modal information drives the gain or one modality supplies a shortcut.

lessons.title: Multimodal AI: Where it can fail
lessons.body: One modality can dominate or introduce new privacy and safety risks.

lessons.title: Multimodal AI: The core idea
lessons.body: Multimodal models align and fuse modalities such as text and images to solve tasks requiring cross-modal understanding.

topics.title: Model optimization
topics.description: Model optimization techniques like quantization, pruning, and distillation reduce latency and memory while preserving acceptable accuracy.

lessons.title: Model optimization: The core idea
lessons.body: Model optimization techniques like quantization, pruning, and distillation reduce latency and memory while preserving acceptable accuracy.

lessons.title: Model optimization: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Benchmark quality, memory, and tail latency on target hardware after each optimization.

topics.title: AI ethics
topics.description: AI ethics addresses fairness, transparency, privacy, and accountability to reduce harm and align systems with human values.

lessons.title: AI ethics: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Principles need concrete indicators and recourse; a checklist alone does not establish fairness.

lessons.title: AI ethics: A worked example
lessons.body: An impact assessment identifies affected groups, plausible harms, mitigations, and owners before launch.

topics.title: End-to-end system
topics.description: An end-to-end AI system integrates data, training, deployment, monitoring, and feedback loops into one reliable production lifecycle.

lessons.title: End-to-end system: The core idea
lessons.body: An end-to-end AI system integrates data, training, deployment, monitoring, and feedback loops into one reliable production lifecycle.

lessons.title: End-to-end system: Test a broken handoff
lessons.body: Walk through a stale feature table or unavailable prediction service and specify what the product does next. Exercise the fallback, alert, and recovery path with a known example. Model quality alone does not determine system reliability when upstream data or downstream actions fail.

lessons.title: End-to-end system: A worked example
lessons.body: Trace a prediction from source data through features and serving to monitoring and user feedback.

lessons.title: End-to-end system: Where it can fail
lessons.body: Failures often occur at handoffs; define ownership, contracts, and recovery across the whole chain.
